# tidyarena

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
<!-- badges: end -->

tidyarena benchmarks dplyr backends against each other with the same dplyr
code. Every task is one pipeline, written once and run unchanged on dplyr,
dtplyr, duckplyr, dbplyr with duckdb, arrow, tidypolars and cuplyr. For each
task it records:

* whether the backend ran it, failed, or fell back to dplyr,
* whether the result matches dplyr's,
* how long it took, including collecting the result into R,
* how much memory it used at its peak.

It also records the machine and its settings (OS, CPU, memory, GPU, disk,
BLAS, thread limits, power settings), so results from many machines can be
compared.

## Installation

You can install the development version of tidyarena from GitHub with:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("bbtheo/tidyarena")
```

Then install the backends you want to compare. `arena_install()` puts them
in a library of their own, so they never mix with your packages:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
tidyarena::arena_install(c("dtplyr", "duckplyr", "dbplyr_duckdb", "arrow"))
```

Packages come as binaries from Posit Package Manager, which builds them for
Windows, macOS and the common Linux distributions (Ubuntu, Debian,
RHEL/Rocky, openSUSE and others). On other x86_64 Linux distributions with
glibc 2.28 or newer, such as Arch or Fedora, it uses Package Manager's
generic `manylinux_2_28` binaries. Those don't cover every package (arrow is
missing, for example). When a package would have to be compiled,
`arena_install()` stops and lists it. Compiling
duckdb or arrow takes a long time and several GB of memory per compile job.
If you want to do it anyway, `build = "capped"` compiles them with a number
of jobs that fits in free memory and, on Linux with systemd, inside a memory
limit with swap disabled.

Backends that are not installed are skipped.

## Usage

See what a run would do, then run it:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(tidyarena)

arena_plan("quick")
run <- arena_run("quick")
arena_report(run)
```

The quick tier runs 23 tasks at 1e6 and 1e7 rows, with one warm-up and
three timed repetitions per task. `"standard"` adds 1e8 rows and `"full"`
adds 1e9.

`arena_report()` shows the fastest backend for every task, and for every
backend its coverage and its time and memory relative to dplyr.
`arena_read()` gives the raw measurements.

## Safe to run

Each task runs in its own R process with a memory budget, by default 70% of
available memory with at least 2 GB left free:

* On Linux with systemd, the budget is a cgroup limit with swap disabled.
  A task that overruns it is killed by the kernel before the machine starts
  swapping.
* On every platform, a watchdog kills a task that goes over budget, leaves
  less than 1 GB free, makes swap grow, or runs too long.
* Sizes that are not expected to fit are skipped before they start, and a
  task that fails at one size is not retried at larger sizes.

Results are written after every task. If a run is interrupted, call
`arena_run(dir = <the run directory>)` to continue it.

## What is measured, and how

* **Data** is generated from a fixed seed, so every machine runs on
  identical tables (see `?arena_data`). It is loaded into each backend's
  own format before timing starts.
* **Time** is the wall time of the pipeline plus `collect()`.
* **Memory** is the peak resident memory of the process. On Linux it is
  exact (the kernel's high-water mark, reset before every repetition);
  elsewhere it is sampled every 0.1 seconds.
* **Correctness** compares a fingerprint of each result with dplyr's: row
  count, column names, missing values, sums and ranges of numeric columns
  (with a relative tolerance), and the distinct values of character
  columns.

Nothing that identifies you or your machine is recorded: no host name, user
name or home directory paths.
